text.p: Time Warner Inc opened down Thursday after Canada's Seagram Co Ltd sold more than half its stake in the company for $1.39 billion.
Shares in Time Warner were off 1-3/8 to 47-1/8 in the opening minutes of trade. Volume was 430,000 shares, putting Time Warner at the top of the New York Stock Exchange's most-active list.
Shares in Seagram, the beverage and entertainment giant, rose one to 39-7/8 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Schroder Wertheim & Co analyst David Londoner said the decline represented a buying opportunity.
"What you have now is a whole bunch of new institutional investors," he said of the Seagram sale.
"I think they're going to find it looks pretty attractive. Anybody who really looks at the company should be impressed."
Dennis McAlpine, analyst at Josephthal Lyon & Ross Inc, attributed the stock drop to fading views of Time Warner as a takeover target.

He said some shareholders had believed the Seagram stake would be sold to one investor who then might launch a bid for the company. However, Merrill had sold the shares to a number of clients, lessening the chance of a swift takeover.
"They thouught the block (of Seagram stock) might facilitate someone else's interest," he said.
